about: A presentation says how one tracker's published output is shown: one tile on Home and one canvas as its full view. It chooses from this kit and binds each block to a field of the output. The tile and the figure block read the output's own value, so both show the same number.

tile.reads: The output's value, state and needs. The label, the mark and the number format come from the presentation. The label and the unit are held to what a tile draws on one line beside its mark. A mark whose binding the output leaves unfilled rests on the tile, and the tracker's canvas says what it needs.

count.reads: A number, written with at most one decimal. The unit is the presentation's own word, or the one the output publishes when it is as short.

money.reads: An amount in the location's currency.

duration.reads: Seconds, written as seconds under a minute and as minutes and seconds from there.

rate.reads: A percentage. A value above 1, or a value published with the unit %, is the percentage itself: 86.5 reads 86.5 %. Any other value from 0 to 1 is a ratio: 0.865 reads 86.5 %.

ranking.name: Products
ranking.needs: Needs events that name a product.

facts.draws: When the tracker last updated, how often it runs and what it watches.
facts.needs: Needs the tracker and its last update.

state_counts.draws: How many shelves are empty, replenished and stocked.

state_cards.draws: One card for each shelf with its state and its times.

ranking.draws: Products in order, each with its count.
ranking.needs: Needs products with a count each.

shapes.rows: A list of {id, at, description}: label may stand for description; product, shelf and at_s are optional. The output's own rows fit, and they carry each row's picture: the host rebuilds them from its records. Of any other list the page reads these fields alone.
shapes.comments: A list of {text}: at (or written_at) places it among the events; id and recommendation are optional. The text slots a tracker's agent writes fit.
shapes.shelves: A list of {shelf, label, state}: state is empty, replenished or stocked; empty_since and replenished_at are optional ISO times.
shapes.ranked: A list of {product, value}: picked, returned and bought are optional.
shapes.readings: The same output over the week, the month and the year, as the tracker's passes store them.
